title: Gaming the IRS’s Third-Party Reporting System: Evidence from Pari-Mutuel Wagering

scopes.description: Complete supplied Stata workflow embedded in Stata Code.pdf: the main race-level pool construction and its T1, T3, and T5–T10/Figure 1 branches, plus the separate T4 IRS state panel. The PDF contains substantive Stata commands but needs extraction/reflow into a working copy and a portable data root. The packaged states data.xlsx matches the T4 code's field contract and can serve as its prepared-input route, bypassing the historical IRS copy/paste step. The T8 comment supports omitting line 600; whether the separate line 602 missing-lnpurse filter is also omitted remains unresolved.

requirements.description: The race-level panel imported as Original1.csv for the main preparation and analyses. The supplied Stata code consumes raw country/date/year/month, purse/distance/runners, track/race/weather/surface fields and the listed pool columns; the actual author export, definitions, period and row coverage are not packaged or specified in the datasheet.

routes.description: The datasheet's acquisition statement names The Jockey Club and Equibase, then describes one dataset obtained from Equibase. The source relationship is not resolved by the package, and no separate Jockey Club input is inferred. This package contains no Original1.csv or compatible race panel; current access, export fields and period remain unknown. The academic-use statement does not establish that the user cannot obtain access.
routes.expected_period: The code uses event dates and year/month, a 2017-09-27 treatment date, 2009-2019 Figure 1 indicators, 2010-2019 T6 indicators and a one-year track lag. The exact source period and required leading coverage are unspecified; 2009 coverage for a 2010 difference is a conditional fidelity check.

requirements.description: Prepared state-by-year IRS input for the supplied T4 construction and loss regression. The code reads State, Sports, Horses, and five measures for each year 2016-2019, then creates a state-year panel.

routes.description: The author describes a prepared IRS table created by copying needed variables into a usable dataset. The packaged workbook has every source header consumed by T4. Its bounded probe reads one row and verifies headers/readability only; full row coverage and output fidelity remain future checks. The code uses a different directory and filename, which can be handled by staging this workbook at that expected path in a working copy.
routes.expected_period: Source measure columns for 2016-2019; the code assigns four years per State and filters by Sports/Horses.

routes.description: The official IRS SOI landing page documents county tables with State totals and a 1989-2022 span, which includes the code's 2016-2019 years (inference). It does not establish the exact itemized-return/nonlimited-dollar fields or the state-year transformations in the prepared workbook. This is an alternative public source route; no data payload was opened or requested.
routes.expected_period: The code uses measures for 2016-2019. The IRS landing page documents a broader year range, but field definitions and construction compatibility remain unverified.

issues.description: Original1.csv, the main race-level panel used by the supplied workflow, is not in this package. The datasheet names The Jockey Club and Equibase in its acquisition statement, then describes one Equibase dataset; the provider relationship is unresolved. The actual export fields/types, exact period/history and present access conditions are unspecified. No evidence establishes a no-license or categorical access barrier.

The T8 comment requires a touchup without the final missing/zero drop and explicitly matches source line 600 (`drop if betratioX == 0 | betratioX == .`). The adjacent line 602 filter (`drop if lnpurse == .`) is separate. Purse is prepared at lines 51–55, and no supplied source establishes that the line 602 exclusion is redundant or that T8 should omit it. Prepare the separate T8 branch without line 600 and retain line 602; whether T8 was intended to include observations excluded by line 602 remains an unresolved sample-scope condition.

The substantive Stata commands are embedded in Stata Code.pdf, not supplied as a standalone do-file. Reflow/extraction into a working copy is needed before an ordinary Stata batch run; this is a preparation step, not evidence that no code was supplied.

The embedded program's global data root is a workstation-specific Windows path. Select a relative data root in a separate working copy and keep the inputs and generated outputs under that root before running.

T4 imports $path/Statetottests/states1.xlsx, whereas the packaged prepared workbook is named states data.xlsx at the package root. Its bounded probe confirms the consumed headers, so stage it at the expected relative location in a working copy; do not treat the filename mismatch as missing IRS data.

The code invokes winsor2, but the supplied environment probe did not find that command in the default or separately configured shared ado paths. Availability outside those checked paths is unknown; no install was attempted.

evidence.description: The datasheet reports a fee and an academic-use understanding for Equibase data, while saying there is no NDA; it does not establish current access or a categorical access barrier.

3. While I do not have a non-disclosure agreement regarding the data or limits on the

evidence.quote:

gen DV = yearbetratioX - lagbetr

evidence.description: Before the separate missing-log-purse filter, the supplied program removes purse commas, destrings purse, and creates lnpurse.

replace purse=subinstr(purse,",","",.)

destring purse, replace

review_notes: The frozen static audit reports no supported code or entry point because extension-only discovery skipped the document-embedded program. Full inspection of the 1,390-line cached Stata Code.pdf text found substantive command blocks for the supplied table and figure workflow; has_code is therefore true and the original PDF is the traceable entry point. The audit remains unchanged and discovery-only.

The datasheet title matches the frozen title in substance; it contains no DOI to conflict with the frozen DOI. The datasheet names both The Jockey Club and Equibase in its acquisition statement, then describes one dataset obtained from Equibase; the exact provider relationship remains unclear. It says public release is inappropriate under an academic-use understanding but also says there is no NDA. Present access and licensing remain unverified; this is not treated as a no-license finding or a confirmed access barrier.

The packaged states data.xlsx is the author-prepared IRS Table 4 workbook: its first-sheet headers match every field consumed by the T4 code. The state and track identifier workbooks are single-column lookups, not full analysis panels. The Stata source hardcodes the track-to-state mapping and imports states1.xlsx, so those lookup sheets are supporting references rather than separate mandatory empirical inputs. The prepared workbook route bypasses the historical IRS download/copy-paste construction.

The T8 comment says to run the touchup without the final missing/zero drop; this matches source line 600, which drops zero/missing betratioX. Separate line 602 drops missing lnpurse. The supplied code prepares purse at lines 51–55, and no supplied evidence says the line 602 filter is redundant or that T8 should omit it. The separate working-copy T8 branch therefore omits line 600 only and retains line 602; exact T8 inclusion of observations excluded by line 602 remains an unresolved sample-scope condition. This is specific to T8 sample definition and does not create an author-approval gate for routine extraction or path setup.

The credential/API/database keyword screen was saved before source display and found no candidate lines; its screen is limited to the listed keyword pattern. Three attempted cats of cached XLSX text failed because their space-containing paths were not shell-quoted; the same exact cached files were then read successfully with quotes. The initial draft initializer also failed because it looked for draft_path in work_item.json instead of the frozen batch assignment. The screening and both incident records are preserved only as unreferenced process evidence and do not support scientific claims.

The work item has no frozen dependency checklist edges; the complete input and generated-file chain is documented in the linked static workflow trace instead of inventing dependency IDs. T7 draws a non-Canada sample with runiform and the supplied source contains no explicit set seed; record this as a result-fidelity context for later comparison, not as an independent missing data input or execution barrier.

The official IRS county-data landing page was opened as static HTML; it documents county data with State totals and a 1989-2022 span. This covers the code's 2016-2019 years by inference but does not demonstrate the exact itemized/nonlimited measure fields or state-year construction. The packaged states data.xlsx remains the selected primary T4 route, and no annual download links or data payloads were opened.

For Equibase/Jockey Club discovery, the frozen lookup helper itself was invoked for Equibase, Jockey and Jockey Club, but all three attempts exited 2 before lookup because the expected sibling resources.py path was missing. A separate saved read-only scan of the exact assigned catalog hash searched those literal terms and found no matching strings. That catalog discovery does not establish missing access, entitlement or licensing; all failed CLI and zero-hit process records and the catalog evidence row remain unreferenced.
